answer: Validators lock 10k copper tokens as collateral and suffer quadratic slashing equal to the square of misbehaved stake, while a zero-knowledge verifiable delay function imposes a 2^20-step delay before finality. Each additional Sybil identity adds an independent lockup, so marginal attack cost grows superlinear O(k^2) and exceeds any extractable reward. The protocol reaches its zenith when the robust Nash equilibrium yields negative expected utility, and the economic forge of consensus remains intact.
